# SEO-609: Serve equivalent primary content on mobile and desktop

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| --- | --- |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

The narrow-viewport rendering of a page contains the same primary content, headings, structured data, metadata, and internal links as the wide-viewport rendering, and does not omit sections or truncate text that only the wide layout shows.

## Rationale

Where indexing is performed from the mobile rendering, content present only in the wide layout is content the index never sees, so the desktop page can be complete while the indexed page is not.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Use one document that reflows rather than two documents selected by device, and where a section is collapsed on narrow screens keep its text in the markup instead of loading it on expand. If a separate mobile host exists, compare its content against the desktop host section by section.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Render each significant route at a narrow and a wide viewport and diff the extracted text, headings, links, structured data, and metadata between them.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `BROWSER`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
